71: /****************************************************************************
72:  * Name: nxtask_assign_pid
73:  *
74:  * Description:
75:  *   This function assigns the next unique task ID to a task.
76:  *
77:  * Input Parameters:
78:  *   tcb - TCB of task
79:  *
80:  * Returned Value:
81:  *   OK on success; ERROR on failure (errno is not set)
82:  *
83:  ****************************************************************************/
84: 
85: static int nxtask_assign_pid(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb)
86: {
87:   FAR struct tcb_s **pidhash;
88:   irqstate_t flags;
89:   pid_t next_pid;
90:   int   hash_ndx;
91:   void *temp;
92:   int   i;
93:   int   ret = -ENOMEM;
94: 
95:   /* NOTE:
96:    * ERROR means that the g_pidhash[] table is completely full.
97:    * We cannot allow another task to be started.
98:    */
99: 
100:   /* We'll try every allowable pid */
101: 
102:   for (; ; )
103:     {
104:       /* Protect the following operation with a critical section
105:        * because g_pidhash is accessed from an interrupt context
106:        */
107: 
108:       flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_pidhashlock);
109: 
110:       /* Get the next process ID candidate */
111: 
112:       next_pid = g_lastpid + 1;
113:       for (i = 0; i < g_npidhash; i++)
114:         {
115:           /* Verify that the next_pid is in the valid range */
116: 
117:           if (next_pid <= 0)
118:             {
119:               next_pid = 1;
120:             }
121: 
122:           /* Get the hash_ndx associated with the next_pid */
123: 
124:           hash_ndx = PIDHASH(next_pid);
125: 
126:           /* Check if there is a (potential) duplicate of this pid */
127: 
128:           if (!g_pidhash[hash_ndx])
129:             {
130:               /* Assign this PID to the task */
131: 
132:               g_pidhash[hash_ndx] = tcb;
133:               tcb->pid = next_pid;
134:               atomic_set(&tcb->refs, 1);
135:               g_lastpid = next_pid;
136: 
137:               spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_pidhashlock, flags);
138:               ret = OK;
139:               break;
140:             }
141: 
142:             next_pid++;
143:         }
144: 
145:       if (ret == OK)
146:         {
147:           break;
148:         }
149: 
150:       /* If we get here, then the g_pidhash[] table is completely full.
151:        * We will alloc new space and copy original g_pidhash to it to
152:        * expand space.
153:        */
154: 
155:       temp = g_pidhash;
156: 
157:       /* Calling malloc in a critical section may cause thread switching.
158:        * Here we check whether other threads have applied successfully,
159:        * and if successful, return directly
160:        */
161: 
162:       spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_pidhashlock, flags);
163:       pidhash = kmm_zalloc((size_t)g_npidhash * 2u * sizeof(*pidhash));
164:       if (pidhash == NULL)
165:         {
166:           ret = -ENOMEM;
167:           break;
168:         }
169: 
170:       /* Handle conner case: context siwtch happened when kmm_malloc */
171: 
172:       flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_pidhashlock);
173:       if (temp != g_pidhash)
174:         {
175:           spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_pidhashlock, flags);
176:           kmm_free(pidhash);
177:           continue;
178:         }
179: 
180:       g_npidhash *= 2;
181: 
182:       /* All original pid and hash_ndx are mismatch,
183:        * so we need to rebuild their relationship
184:        */
185: 
186:       for (i = 0; i < g_npidhash / 2; i++)
187:         {
188:           if (g_pidhash[i] == NULL)
189:             {
190:               /* If the pid is not used, skip it.
191:                * This may be triggered when a context switch occurs
192:                * during zalloc and a thread is destroyed.
193:                */
194: 
195:               continue;
196:             }
197: 
198:           hash_ndx = PIDHASH(g_pidhash[i]->pid);
199:           DEBUGASSERT(pidhash[hash_ndx] == NULL);
200:           pidhash[hash_ndx] = g_pidhash[i];
201:         }
202: 
203:       /* Release resource for original g_pidhash, using new g_pidhash */
204: 
205:       g_pidhash = pidhash;
206:       spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_pidhashlock, flags);
207:       kmm_free(temp);
208: 
209:       /* Let's try every allowable pid again */
210:     }
211: 
212:   return ret;
213: }

215: /****************************************************************************
216:  * Name: nxtask_inherit_affinity
217:  *
218:  * Description:
219:  *   exec(), task_create(), and vfork() all inherit the affinity mask from
220:  *   the parent thread.  This is the default for pthread_create() as well
221:  *   but the affinity mask can be specified in the pthread attributes as
222:  *   well.  pthread_setup() will have to fix up the affinity mask in this
223:  *   case.
224:  *
225:  * Input Parameters:
226:  *   tcb - The TCB of the new task.
227:  *
228:  * Returned Value:
229:  *   None
230:  *
231:  * Assumptions:
232:  *   The parent of the new task is the task at the head of the assigned task
233:  *   list for the current CPU.
234:  *
235:  ****************************************************************************/
236: 
237: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
238: static inline void nxtask_inherit_affinity(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb)
239: {
240:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
241:   tcb->affinity = rtcb->affinity;

247: /****************************************************************************
248:  * Name: nxtask_save_parent
249:  *
250:  * Description:
251:  *   Save the task ID of the parent task in the child task's group and
252:  *   allocate a child status structure to catch the child task's exit
253:  *   status.
254:  *
255:  * Input Parameters:
256:  *   tcb   - The TCB of the new, child task.
257:  *   ttype - Type of the new thread: task, pthread, or kernel thread
258:  *
259:  * Returned Value:
260:  *   None
261:  *
262:  * Assumptions:
263:  *   The parent of the new task is the task at the head of the ready-to-run
264:  *   list.
265:  *
266:  ****************************************************************************/
267: 
268: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_HAVE_PARENT
269: static inline void nxtask_save_parent(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, int ttype)
270: {
271:   DEBUGASSERT(tcb != NULL && tcb->group != NULL);
272: 
273:   /* Only newly created tasks (and kernel threads) have parents.  None of
274:    * this logic applies to pthreads with reside in the same group as the
275:    * parent and share that same child/parent relationships.
276:    */
277: 
278: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PTHREAD
279:   if ((atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK) !=
280:       TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD)
281: #endif
282:     {
283:       /* Get the TCB of the parent task.  In this case, the calling task. */
284: 
285:       FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
286: 
287:       DEBUGASSERT(rtcb != NULL && rtcb->group != NULL);
288: 
289:       /* Save the PID of the parent tasks' task group in the child's task
290:        * group.  Copy the ID from the parent's task group structure to
291:        * child's task group.
292:        */
293: 
294:       tcb->group->tg_ppid = rtcb->group->tg_pid;
295: 
296: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_CHILD_STATUS
297:       /* Tasks can also suppress retention of their child status by applying
298:        * the SA_NOCLDWAIT flag with sigaction().
299:        */
300: 
301:       if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->group->tg_flags) & GROUP_FLAG_NOCLDWAIT) == 0)
302:         {
303:           FAR struct child_status_s *child;
304: 
305:           /* Make sure that there is not already a structure for this PID in
306:            * the parent TCB.  There should not be.
307:            */
308: 
309:           child = group_find_child(rtcb->group, tcb->pid);
310:           DEBUGASSERT(child == NULL);
311:           if (child == NULL)
312:             {
313:               /* Allocate a new status structure  */
314: 
315:               child = group_alloc_child();
316:             }
317: 
318:           /* Did we successfully find/allocate the child status structure? */
319: 
320:           DEBUGASSERT(child != NULL);
321:           if (child != NULL)
322:             {
323:               /* Yes.. Initialize the structure */
324: 
325:               child->ch_flags  = ttype;
326:               child->ch_pid    = tcb->pid;
327:               child->ch_status = 0;
328: 
329:               /* Add the entry into the group's list of children */
330: 
331:               group_add_child(rtcb->group, child);
332:             }
333:         }
334: 
335: #else /* CONFIG_SCHED_CHILD_STATUS */
336:       /* Child status is not retained.  Simply keep track of the number
337:        * child tasks created.
338:        */
339: 
340:       DEBUGASSERT(atomic_read(&rtcb->group->tg_nchildren) < UINT16_MAX);
341: 
342:       atomic_add_relaxed(&rtcb->group->tg_nchildren, 1);
343: 
344: #endif /* CONFIG_SCHED_CHILD_STATUS */
345:     }
346: }
347: #else
348: #  define nxtask_save_parent(tcb,ttype)
349: #endif

351: /****************************************************************************
352:  * Name: nxtask_dup_dspace
353:  *
354:  * Description:
355:  *   When a new task or thread is created from a PIC module, then that
356:  *   module (probably) intends the task or thread to execute in the same
357:  *   D-Space.  This function will duplicate the D-Space for that purpose.
358:  *
359:  * Input Parameters:
360:  *   tcb - The TCB of the new task.
361:  *
362:  * Returned Value:
363:  *   None
364:  *
365:  * Assumptions:
366:  *   The parent of the new task is the task at the head of the ready-to-run
367:  *   list.
368:  *
369:  ****************************************************************************/
370: 
371: #ifdef CONFIG_PIC
372: static inline void nxtask_dup_dspace(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb)
373: {
374:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
375:   if (rtcb->dspace != NULL)
376:     {
377:       /* Copy the D-Space structure reference and increment the reference
378:        * count on the memory.  The D-Space memory will persist until the
379:        * last thread exits (see nxsched_release_tcb()).
380:        */
381: 
382:       tcb->dspace = rtcb->dspace;
383:       tcb->dspace->crefs++;
384:     }
385: }
386: #else
387: #  define nxtask_dup_dspace(tcb)
388: #endif

390: /****************************************************************************
391:  * Name: nxthread_setup_scheduler
392:  *
393:  * Description:
394:  *   This functions initializes the common portions of the Task Control Block
395:  *   (TCB) in preparation for starting a new thread.
396:  *
397:  *   nxthread_setup_scheduler() is called from nxtask_setup_scheduler() and
398:  *   pthread_setup_scheduler().
399:  *
400:  * Input Parameters:
401:  *   tcb        - Address of the new task's TCB
402:  *   priority   - Priority of the new task
403:  *   start      - Thread startup routine
404:  *   entry      - Thread user entry point
405:  *   ttype      - Type of the new thread: task, pthread, or kernel thread
406:  *
407:  * Returned Value:
408:  *   OK on success; ERROR on failure.
409:  *
410:  *   This function can only failure is it is unable to assign a new, unique
411:  *   task ID to the TCB (errno is not set).
412:  *
413:  ****************************************************************************/
414: 
415: static int nxthread_setup_scheduler(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, int priority,
416:                                     start_t start, CODE void *entry,
417:                                     int ttype)
418: {
419:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
420:   irqstate_t flags;
421:   int ret;
422: 
423:   /* Assign a unique task ID to the task. */
424: 
425:   ret = nxtask_assign_pid(tcb);
426:   if (ret == OK)
427:     {
428:       struct tls_info_s *info = tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
429: 
430:       /* Save PID to TLS */
431: 
432:       info->tl_tid = tcb->pid;
433: 
434:       /* Save task priority and entry point in the TCB */
435: 
436:       tcb->sched_priority = priority;
437:       tcb->init_priority  = priority;
438: #ifdef CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE
439:       tcb->base_priority  = (uint8_t)priority;
440: #endif
441:       tcb->start          = start;
442:       tcb->entry.main     = (main_t)entry;
443: 
444:       /* Save the thread type.  This setting will be needed in
445:        * up_initial_state() is called.
446:        */
447: 
448:       ttype              &= TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK;
449:       atomic_and(&tcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK);
450:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, ttype);
451: 
452:       /* Set the appropriate scheduling policy in the TCB */
453: 
454:       atomic_and(&tcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK);
455: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
456:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR);
457:       tcb->timeslice      = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
458: #else
459:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_FIFO);
460: #endif
461: 
462:       /* Save the task ID of the parent task in the TCB and allocate
463:        * a child status structure.
464:        */
465: 
466:       nxtask_save_parent(tcb, ttype);
467: 
468: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
469:       /* exec(), task_create(), and vfork() all inherit the affinity mask
470:        * from the parent thread.  This is the default for pthread_create()
471:        * as well but the affinity mask can be specified in the pthread
472:        * attributes as well.  pthread_create() will have to fix up the
473:        * affinity mask in this case.
474:        */
475: 
476:       nxtask_inherit_affinity(tcb);
477: #endif
478: 
479:       /* exec(), pthread_create(), task_create(), and vfork() all
480:        * inherit the signal mask of the parent thread.
481:        */
482: 
483:       tcb->sigprocmask = rtcb->sigprocmask;
484: 
485:       /* Initialize the task state.  It does not get a valid state
486:        * until it is activated.
487:        */
488: 
489:       tcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_INVALID;
490: 
491:       /* Clone the parent tasks D-Space (if it was running PIC).  This
492:        * must be done before calling up_initial_state() so that the
493:        * state setup will take the PIC address base into account.
494:        */
495: 
496:       nxtask_dup_dspace(tcb);
497:

52:  *   the thread thread to the CPU set pointed to by cpuset.  If the call
53:  *   is successful, and the thread is not currently running on one of the
54:  *   CPUs in cpuset, then it is migrated to one of those CPUs.
55: 
56:  *   The argument cpusetsize is the length (in bytes) of the buffer
57:  *   pointed to by cpuset.  Typically, this argument would be specified as
58:  *   sizeof(cpu_set_t).

67:  *   nature of the failure.

69:  ****************************************************************************/

71: int pthread_setaffinity_np(pthread_t thread, size_t cpusetsize,
72:                            FAR const cpu_set_t *cpuset)

83:    * value.

49:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
50:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
51:  *
52:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
53:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
54:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
55:  *
56:  *   nxsched_set_affinity() is identical to the function sched_setparam(),
57:  *   differing only in its return value:  This function does not modify
58:  *   the errno variable.  This is a non-standard, internal OS function and
59:  *   is not intended for use by application logic.  Applications should
60:  *   use the standard sched_setparam().
61:  *
62:  * Input Parameters:
63:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
64:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
65:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
66:  *
67:  * Returned Value:
68:  *   Zero (OK) if successful.  Otherwise, a negated errno value is returned:
69:  *
70:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
71:  *
72:  ****************************************************************************/
73: 
74: int nxsched_set_affinity(pid_t pid, size_t cpusetsize,
75:                          FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
76: {
77:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb;
78:   irqstate_t flags;
79:   int ret = OK;
80: 
81:   DEBUGASSERT(cpusetsize == sizeof(cpu_set_t) && mask != NULL);
82: 
83:   /* Make sure that affinity mask is valid */
84: 
85:   if (*mask == 0)
86:     {
87:       return -EINVAL;
88:     }
89: 
90:   /* Verify that the PID corresponds to a real task */
91: 
92:   if (!pid)
93:     {
94:       tcb = this_task();
95:     }
96:   else
97:     {
98:       tcb = nxsched_get_tcb(pid);
99:     }
100: 
101:   if (tcb == NULL)
102:     {
103:       ret = -ESRCH;
104:       goto errout;
105:     }
106: 
107:   /* Don't permit changing the affinity mask of any task locked to a CPU
108:    * (i.e., an IDLE task)
109:    */
110: 
111:   flags = enter_critical_section();
112:   if ((atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) != 0)
113:     {
114:       ret = -EINVAL;
115:       goto errout_with_csection;
116:     }
117: 
118:   /* Set the new affinity mask. */
119: 
120:   tcb->affinity = *mask;
121: 
122:   /* Is the task still executing a a CPU in its affinity mask? Will this
123:    * change cause the task to be removed from its current assigned task
124:    * list?
125:    *
126:    * First... is the task in an assigned task list?
127:    */
128: 
129:   if (tcb->task_state >= FIRST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE &&
130:       tcb->task_state <= LAST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE)
131:     {
132:       /* Yes... is the CPU associated with the assigned task in the new
133:        * affinity mask?
134:        */
135: 
136:       if ((tcb->affinity & (1 << tcb->cpu)) == 0)
137:         {
138:           /* No.. then we will need to move the task from the assigned
139:            * task list to some other ready to run list.
140:            *
141:            * nxsched_set_priority() will do just what we want... it will
142:            * remove the task from its current position in the some assigned
143:            * task list and then simply put it back in the right place.  This
144:            * works even if the task is this task.
145:            */
146: 
147:           ret = nxsched_set_priority(tcb, tcb->sched_priority);
148:         }
149:     }
150: 
151: errout_with_csection:
152:   leave_critical_section(flags);
153:   if (pid)
154:     {
155:       nxsched_put_tcb(tcb);
156:     }
157: 
158: errout:
159:   return ret;
160: }

162: /****************************************************************************
163:  * Name: sched_setaffinity
164:  *
165:  * Description:
166:  *   sched_setaffinity() sets the CPU affinity mask of the thread whose ID
167:  *   is pid to the value specified by mask.  If pid is zero, then the
168:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
169:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
170:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
171:  *
172:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
173:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
174:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
175:  *
176:  *   This function is a simply wrapper around nxsched_set_affinity() that
177:  *   sets the errno value in the event of an error.
178:  *
179:  * Input Parameters:
180:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
181:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
182:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
183:  *
184:  * Returned Value:
185:  *   0 if successful.  Otherwise, ERROR (-1) is returned, and errno is
186:  *   set appropriately:
187:  *
188:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
189:  *
190:  ****************************************************************************/
191: 
192: int sched_setaffinity(pid_t pid, size_t cpusetsize,
193:                       FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
194: {
195:   int ret = nxsched_set_affinity(pid, cpusetsize, mask);
196:   if (ret < 0)
197:     {
198:       set_errno(-ret);
199:       ret = ERROR;
200:     }
201: 
202:   return ret;
203: }

58:  *   execution of a task.  It receives initial control when the task is
59:  *   started and calls main entry point of the newly started task.
60:  *
61:  * Input Parameters:
62:  *   None
63:  *
64:  * Returned Value:
65:  *   None
66:  *

69: void nxtask_start(void)
70: {
71:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = this_task();
72:   int ttype = atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK;
73:   main_t entry_main = tcb->entry.main;
74:   int exitcode = EXIT_FAILURE;
75:   FAR char **argv;
76:   int argc;
77: 
78:   DEBUGASSERT(ttype != TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
79: 
80: #ifdef CONFIG_SIG_DEFAULT
81:   if (ttype != TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL)
82:     {
83:       /* Set up default signal actions for NON-kernel thread */
84: 
85:       nxsig_default_initialize(tcb);
86:     }
87: #endif
88: 
89:   /* Take args from stack, as group is shared for kthreads */
90: 
91:   argv = nxsched_get_stackargs(tcb);
92:   for (argc = 0; argv && argv[argc]; argc++);
93: 
94:   /* Call the 'main' entry point passing argc and argv.  In the kernel build
95:    * this has to be handled differently if we are starting a user-space task;
96:    * we have to switch to user-mode before calling the task.
97:    */
98: 
99:   if (ttype == TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL)
100:     {
101:       exitcode = entry_main(argc, argv);
102:     }
103:   else
104:     {
105: #ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT
106:       up_addrenv_leave_kernel();
107:       nxtask_startup(entry_main, argc, argv);
108: #else
109:       up_task_start(entry_main, argc, argv);
110: #endif
111:     }
112: 
113:   /* Call _exit() if/when the task returns */
114: 
115:   _exit(exitcode);

220: static void mb_ipc_task( void *para )
221: {
222: 	bk_err_t	ret_val;
223: 	u32    events;
224: 	u32    check_time = BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER;
225: 
226: 	mb_ipc_init_lv_callback();
227: 
228: 	ret_val = rtos_init_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event);
229: 
230: 	if(ret_val != BK_OK)
231: 	{
232: 		rtos_delete_thread(NULL);
233: 		return;
234: 	}
235: 
236: 	while(1)
237: 	{
238: 		events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_ALL_FLAGS, true, check_time);
239: 
240: 		if(events == 0)
241: 		{
242: 			// timeout, so check heartbeat.
243: 			events = MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG;
244: 		}
245: 
246: 		if(events & MB_IPC_STOP_CORE_FLAG)  // process this event at first!!!!
247: 		{
248: 			if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
249: 			{
250: 				events = 0;  // clear all events.
251: 			}
252: 		}
253: 
254: 		if(events & MB_IPC_START_CORE_FLAG)
255: 		{
256: 			u8   retry_cnt = 0;
257: 
258: 			while(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
259: 			{
260: 				ipc_heartbeat_timeout();
261: 
262: 				if(events & MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG)
263: 				{
264: 					if(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
265: 					{
266: 						cpu_x_state = CORE_POWER_ON;
267: 						break;  // cpu1 power on.
268: 					}
269: 				}
270: 				else
271: 				{
272: 					if( retry_cnt > 3)
273: 					{
274: 						BK_DUMP_OUT("IPC retry to start core%d, retry_cnt:%d\r\n", cpu_x_id, retry_cnt);
275: 						bk_pm_openvela_mailbox_diag_dump();
276: 						// restart_cpu_x();
277: 						break;
278: 					}
279: 					else
280: 					{
281: 						events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG, true, 2000);//2s
282: 					}
283: 				}
284: 
285: 				retry_cnt++;
286: 			}
287: 
288: 			// discard this event when not in CORE_STARTING state.
289: 		}
290: 
291: 		if(events & MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG)
292: 		{
293: 			if(ipc_heartbeat_timeout())
294: 			{
295: 				BK_LOGE(MOD_TAG, "IPC[%d]heartbeat timeout %d,%d\r\n",cpu_x_id,cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp,(u32)rtos_get_time());
296: 				/*when cpu1 heartbeat timeout, then system reboot*/
297: 				cpu_x_heartbeat_timeout = 1;
298: 				ap_console_bridge_link_down();
299: 				BK_ASSERT(false);
300: 			}
301: 		}
302: 
303: 		if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
304: 		{
305: 			check_time = BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER;
306: 		}
307: 		else
308: 		{
309: 			check_time = HB_TIMEOUT_MS;
310: 		}
311: 	}
312: }

57: static void mbox0_reap_slots(u8 dst)
58: {
59: 	mbox0_tx_slots_t *slots;
60: 	uint32_t fifo_count;
61: 	u32 reaped = 0;
62: 	u32 now;
63: 	u8 i;
64: 
65: 	if (mbox0_drv_get_send_count(dst, &fifo_count) != MBOX0_HAL_OK)
66: 		return;
67: 
68: 	slots = &mailbox_slots[dst];
69: 	if (fifo_count != 0)
70: 	{
71: 		slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = 0;
72: 		return;
73: 	}
74: 
75: 	now = rtos_get_time();
76: 	if (!slots->fifo_empty_since_ms)
77: 	{
78: 		slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = now ? now : 1;
79: 		return;
80: 	}
81: 	if ((u32)(now - slots->fifo_empty_since_ms) <
82: 		MBOX0_SLOT_QUARANTINE_MS)
83: 		return;
84: 
85: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_CMD_SLOT_NUM; i++)
86: 	{
87: 		reaped += slots->cmd_used[i] != 0;
88: 		slots->cmd_used[i] = 0;
89: 	}
90: 	/* The hardware FIFO contains pointers into these slots.  Once it has
91: 	 * remained empty for the quarantine interval, the peer has had ample time
92: 	 * to copy every published entry.  ACK-only AP traffic has no later command
93: 	 * fence, so retaining these slots indefinitely exhausts the pool during
94: 	 * RESET/STATE/PWC bring-up.
95: 	 */
96: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_ACK_SLOT_NUM; i++)
97: 	{
98: 		reaped += slots->ack_used[i] != 0;
99: 		slots->ack_used[i] = 0;
100: 	}
101: 	reaped += slots->reset_used != 0;
102: 	reaped += slots->sync_used != 0;
103: 	slots->reset_used = 0;
104: 	slots->sync_used = 0;
105: 	slots->cmd_active = 0;
106: 	slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = 0;
107: 	adapter_diag.tx_reaped += reaped;
108: }

110: static bool mbox0_rx_ready(void)
111: {

115: static mbox0_rx_desc_t *mbox0_oldest_desc(bool priority)
116: {
117: 	mbox0_rx_desc_t *oldest = NULL;
118: 	u8 i;
119: 
120: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_RX_DESC_NUM; i++)
121: 	{
122: 		u8 ctrl;
123: 
124: 		if (!rx_desc[i].used)
125: 			continue;
126: 		ctrl = (rx_desc[i].data.param0 >> 12) & 0x0f;
127: 		if (((ctrl & MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX) != 0) != priority)
128: 			continue;
129: 		if (!oldest || (int32_t)(rx_desc[i].order - oldest->order) < 0)
130: 			oldest = &rx_desc[i];
131: 	}
132: 	return oldest;
133: }

135: static mbox0_stable_slot_t *mbox0_alloc_slot(u8 dst, u8 ctrl,
136: 					     u8 *kind, u8 *index)
137: {
138: 	mbox0_tx_slots_t *slots = &mailbox_slots[dst];
139: 	u8 i;
140: 
141: 	if (ctrl == (MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX | MBOX0_CTRL_RESET))
142: 	{
143: 		if (slots->reset_used)
144: 			return NULL;
145: 		slots->reset_used = 1;
146: 		slots->reset_order = ++slots->publish_order;
147: 		*kind = 2;
148: 		return &slots->reset;
149: 	}
150: 
151: 	if (ctrl & MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX)
152: 	{
153: 		for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_ACK_SLOT_NUM; i++)
154: 		{
155: 			if (!slots->ack_used[i])
156: 			{
157: 				slots->ack_used[i] = 1;
158: 				slots->ack_order[i] = ++slots->publish_order;
159: 				*kind = 1;
160: 				*index = i;
161: 				return &slots->ack[i];
162: 			}
163: 		}
164: 		return NULL;
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	if (ctrl == MBOX0_CTRL_SYNC_TX)
168: 	{
169: 		if (slots->sync_used)
170: 			return NULL;
171: 		slots->sync_used = 1;
172: 		slots->sync_order = ++slots->publish_order;
173: 		*kind = 3;
174: 		return &slots->sync;
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_CMD_SLOT_NUM; i++)
178: 	{
179: 		if (!slots->cmd_used[i])
180: 		{
181: 			slots->cmd_used[i] = 1;
182: 			slots->cmd_order[i] = ++slots->publish_order;
183: 			slots->cmd_active = i + 1;
184: 			*kind = 0;
185: 			*index = i;
186: 			return &slots->cmd[i];
187: 		}
188: 	}
189: 
190: 	return NULL;
191: }

193: static void mbox0_release_slot(u8 dst, u8 kind, u8 index)
194: {
195: 	mbox0_tx_slots_t *slots = &mailbox_slots[dst];
196: 
197: 	if (kind == 0)
198: 	{
199: 		slots->cmd_used[index] = 0;
200: 		if (slots->cmd_active == index + 1)
201: 			slots->cmd_active = 0;
202: 	}
203: 	else if (kind == 1)
204: 		slots->ack_used[index] = 0;
205: 	else if (kind == 2)
206: 		slots->reset_used = 0;
207: 	else
208: 		slots->sync_used = 0;
209: }

211: void bk_mailbox_poll(void)
212: {
213: 	u8 dst;
214: 
215: 	u32 flags = rtos_disable_int();
216: 	for (dst = 0; dst < MBOX_CHNL_NUM; dst++)
217: 	{
218: 		if (dst != MAILBOX_CPU0)
219: 			mbox0_reap_slots(dst);
220: 	}
221: 	mbox0_drv_poll();
222: 	rtos_enable_int(flags);
223: 
224: 	while (1)
225: 	{
226: 		mbox0_rx_desc_t desc;
227: 		mbox0_rx_desc_t *selected;
228: 
229: 		flags = rtos_disable_int();
230: 		if (!rx_count)
231: 		{
232: 			rtos_enable_int(flags);
233: 			break;
234: 		}
235: 		selected = mbox0_oldest_desc(true);
236: 		if (!selected)
237: 			selected = mbox0_oldest_desc(false);
238: 		if (!selected ||
239: 			(((selected->data.param0 >> 12) & MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX) == 0 &&
240: 			 upper_rx_ready && !upper_rx_ready()))
241: 		{
242: 			rtos_enable_int(flags);
243: 			break;
244: 		}
245: 		desc = *selected;
246: 		selected->used = 0;
247: 		rx_count--;
248: 		rtos_enable_int(flags);
249: 		if (mailbox_callback[desc.source])
250: 			mailbox_callback[desc.source](&desc.data);
251: 
252: 		flags = rtos_disable_int();
253: 		mbox0_drv_poll();
254: 		rtos_enable_int(flags);
255: 	}
256: }

258: static void mbox0_rx_isr(mbox0_message_t *msg)
259: {
260: 	u32 address;
261: 	u32 source;
262: 	u32 reaped = 0;
263: 	mbox0_rx_desc_t *desc;
264: 	u8 ctrl;
265: 	u8 i;
266: 
267: 	if (!msg)
268: 		return;
269: 
270: 	source = msg->src_cpu;
271: 	if (source != MAILBOX_CPU1)
272: 	{
273: 		adapter_diag.bad_sid++;
274: 		return;
275: 	}
276: 	if (msg->data[1] != sizeof(mailbox_data_t))
277: 	{
278: 		adapter_diag.bad_length++;
279: 		return;
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	address = msg->data[0];
283: 	if (address & 0x3u)
284: 	{
285: 		adapter_diag.bad_alignment++;
286: 		return;
287: 	}
288: 	if (address > UINT32_MAX - sizeof(mailbox_data_t) ||
289: 		address < MBOX0_AP_RAM_START ||
290: 		address + sizeof(mailbox_data_t) > MBOX0_AP_RAM_END)
291: 	{
292: 		adapter_diag.bad_address++;
293: 		return;
294: 	}
295: 	if (rx_count >= MBOX0_RX_DESC_NUM)
296: 	{
297: 		adapter_diag.descriptor_overflow++;
298: 		return;
299: 	}
300: 
301: #if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
302: 	SCB_InvalidateDCache_by_Addr((void *)address, sizeof(mailbox_data_t));
303: #endif
304: 	__DMB();
305: 	desc = NULL;
306: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_RX_DESC_NUM; i++)
307: 	{
308: 		if (!rx_desc[i].used)
309: 		{
310: 			desc = &rx_desc[i];
311: 			break;
312: 		}
313: 	}
314: 	if (!desc)
315: 	{
316: 		adapter_diag.descriptor_overflow++;
317: 		return;
318: 	}
319: 	memcpy(&desc->data, (void *)address, sizeof(desc->data));
320: 	adapter_diag.last_rx_header = desc->data.param0;
321: 	ctrl = (desc->data.param0 >> 12) & 0x0f;
322: 	if ((ctrl & MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX) == 0)
323: 	{
324: 		adapter_diag.last_cmd_header = desc->data.param0;
325: 		adapter_diag.cmd_received++;
326: 	}
327: 	if (ctrl == 0)
328: 	{
329: 		/* AP serializes ordinary logical commands.  Receiving the next one
330: 		 * proves that it copied the preceding CP transport ACK, providing an
331: 		 * exact lifetime fence even during a continuous UART/PWC burst. */
332: 		for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_ACK_SLOT_NUM; i++)
333: 		{
334: 			reaped += mailbox_slots[source].ack_used[i] != 0;
335: 			mailbox_slots[source].ack_used[i] = 0;
336: 		}
337: 		adapter_diag.tx_reaped += reaped;
338: 	}
339: 	desc->source = source;
340: 	desc->order = ++rx_order;
341: 	desc->used = 1;
342: 	rx_count++;
343: 	adapter_diag.rx_accepted++;
344: 
345: 	/* The vendor adapter dispatches the logical callback from the mailbox
346: 	 * receive path.  Keep ACK generation in the same interrupt transaction;
347: 	 * delaying it until mb_chnl_poll() can stall AP bring-up. */
348: 	if (mailbox_callback[source] != NULL)
349: 	{
350: 		adapter_diag.callback_called++;
351: 		mailbox_callback[source](&desc->data);
352: 	}
353: 	else
354: 		adapter_diag.callback_missing++;
355: 
356: 	desc->used = 0;
357: 	rx_count--;
358: 
359: }

391: bk_err_t bk_mailbox_send(mailbox_data_t *data, mailbox_endpoint_t src,
392: 			 mailbox_endpoint_t dst, void *arg)
393: {
394: 	mbox0_message_t message;
395: 	mbox0_stable_slot_t *slot;
396: 	uint32_t fifo_status;
397: 	u8 ctrl;
398: 	u8 kind = 0;
399: 	u8 index = 0;
400: 	int ret_code;
401: 
402: 	(void)arg;
403: 	if (src != MAILBOX_CPU0 || dst >= MBOX_CHNL_NUM)
404: 		return BK_ERR_MAILBOX_SRC_DST;
405: 	if (!data)
406: 		return BK_ERR_NULL_PARAM;
407: 
408: 	ret_code = mbox0_drv_get_send_stat(dst, &fifo_status);
409: 	if (ret_code != MBOX0_HAL_OK)
410: 		return BK_ERR_MAILBOX_SRC_DST;
411: 	if (fifo_status & RX_FIFO_STAT_FULL)
412: 		return BK_ERR_MAILBOX_TIMEOUT;
413: 
414: 	ctrl = (data->param0 >> 12) & 0x0f;
415: 	mbox0_reap_slots(dst);
416: 	slot = mbox0_alloc_slot(dst, ctrl, &kind, &index);
417: 	if (!slot)
418: 	{
419: 		adapter_diag.tx_slot_busy++;
420: 		return BK_ERR_BUSY;
421: 	}
422: 
423: 	memset(slot, 0, sizeof(*slot));
424: 	memcpy(&slot->data, data, sizeof(slot->data));
425: 	mailbox_slots[dst].fifo_empty_since_ms = 0;
426: #if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
427: 	SCB_CleanDCache_by_Addr((u32 *)slot, sizeof(*slot));
428: #endif
429: 	__DMB();
430: 	message.data[0] = (u32)&slot->data;
431: 	message.data[1] = sizeof(slot->data);
432: 	message.dest_cpu = dst;
433: 	ret_code = mbox0_drv_send_message(&message);
434: 	if (ret_code != MBOX0_HAL_OK)
435: 	{
436: 		mbox0_release_slot(dst, kind, index);
437: 		if (ctrl & MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX)
438: 			adapter_diag.ack_send_fail++;
439: 		return BK_ERR_MAILBOX_NOT_INIT;
440: 	}
441: 	if (ctrl == MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX)
442: 	{
443: 		adapter_diag.last_ack_header = slot->data.param0;
444: 		adapter_diag.ack_sent++;
445: 	}
446: 	return BK_OK;
447: }

    feat: complete BK7258 mailbox console integration
    
    Integrate the BK7258 OpenVela AP with the Beken CP through the UART0 Mailbox V2 full-duplex bridge. Add AP mailbox serial support, transport ACK/RESET/probe recovery, IPC and PWC readiness gates, heartbeat link-down handling, PSRAM layout validation, and board bring-up integration.
    
    Add the CP AP_CONSOLE owner state machine, bounded raw input/output bridge, diagnostics, link recovery, and Ctrl-] exit sequence handling. The exit sequence accepts Ctrl-] followed by releasing the key and pressing '.', without depending on the AP line-editing state.
    
    Enable NuttX CLE editing, command history, TTY SIGINT, foreground builtin applications, and the contest-local ctrlc_test application for validating Ctrl-C over the physical UART0 path.
    
    Document reproducible UART console commands, direct-copy command blocks, AP-to-CP exit key order, external AVDK synchronization, build verification, and the validated AP/package SHA256 values. Preserve the authoritative CP override files under external/bk_avdk_smp and keep public workspace repositories out of the commit.

240: /****************************************************************************
241:  * Public Functions
242:  ****************************************************************************/
243: 
244: /****************************************************************************
245:  * Name:  nxsched_set_priority
246:  *
247:  * Description:
248:  *   This function sets the priority of a specified task.
249:  *
250:  *   NOTE: Setting a task's priority to the same value has a similar effect
251:  *   to sched_yield() -- The task will be moved to after all other tasks
252:  *   with the same priority.
253:  *
254:  * Input Parameters:
255:  *   tcb - the TCB of task to reprioritize.
256:  *   sched_priority - The new task priority
257:  *
258:  * Returned Value:
259:  *   On success, nxsched_set_priority() returns 0 (OK). On error, a negated
260:  *   errno value is returned.
261:  *
262:  *  EINVAL The parameter 'param' is invalid or does not make sense for the
263:  *         current scheduling policy.
264:  *  EPERM  The calling task does not have appropriate privileges.
265:  *  ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
266:  *
267:  ****************************************************************************/
268: 
269: int nxsched_set_priority(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, int sched_priority)
270: {
271:   irqstate_t flags;
272:   int ret = OK;
273: 
274:   /* Verify that the requested priority is in the valid range */
275: 
276:   if (sched_priority >= SCHED_PRIORITY_MIN &&
277:       sched_priority <= SCHED_PRIORITY_MAX)
278:     {
279:       /* We need to assure that there there is no interrupt activity while
280:        * performing the following.
281:        */
282: 
283:       flags = enter_critical_section();
284: 
285:       /* There are three major cases (and two sub-cases) that must be
286:        * considered:
287:        */
288: 
289:       switch (tcb->task_state)
290:         {
291:           /* CASE 1. The task is running and a context switch may be caused
292:            * by the re-prioritization
293:            */
294: 
295:           case TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING:
296:             nxsched_running_setpriority(tcb, sched_priority);
297:             break;
298: 
299:           /* CASE 2. The task is ready-to-run (but not running) and a context
300:            * switch may be caused by the re-prioritization
301:            */
302: 
303:           case TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN:
304:             nxsched_readytorun_setpriority(tcb, sched_priority);
305:             break;
306: 
307:           /* CASE 3. The task is not in the ready to run list.  Changing its
308:            * Priority cannot effect the currently executing task.
309:            */
310: 
311:           default:
312:             nxsched_blocked_setpriority(tcb, sched_priority);
313:             break;
314:         }
315: 
316:       leave_critical_section(flags);
317:     }
318:   else
319:     {
320:       ret = -EINVAL;
321:     }
322: 
323:   return ret;
324: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 AP_SPINLOCK-backed software hwspinlock.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: 
11: #include <nuttx/hwspinlock/hwspinlock.h>
12: 
13: #include "arm_internal.h"
14: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
15: 
16: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY       0xa1000000u
17: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER     0xa2000000u
18: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY  0xa3000000u
19: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT      0xa4000000u
20: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT    0xa5000000u
21: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED    0xa6000000u
22: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK      0xa7000000u
23: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED    0xa8000000u
24: 
25: struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s
26: {
27:   volatile uint32_t interested[2];
28:   volatile uint32_t turn;
29:   volatile uint32_t owner;
30:   volatile uint32_t depth;
31: };
32: 
33: static struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s g_bk7258_atomic_gate
34:   __attribute__((section(".bk_spinlock"), aligned(32)));
35: 
36: static inline void bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(unsigned int cpu, uint32_t value)
37: {
38:   if (cpu == 0 && (bk7258_boottrace_words()[6] & 0xffu) == 2u)
39:     {
40:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
45: {
46:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
47:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
48: 
49:   (void)dev;
50:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
51:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
52: 
53:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
54:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
55:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
56:    */
57: 
58:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
59:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
60:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
61:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
62:    */
63: 
64:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
65:     {
66:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
67:         {
68:           PANIC();
69:         }
70: 
71:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
72:       UP_DMB();
73:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
74:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
75:       return true;
76:     }
77: 
78:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
79:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
80:    */
81: 
82:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
83:     {
84:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
85:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
86:       return false;
87:     }
88: 
89:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
90:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
91:    * one-attempt contract.
92:    */
93: 
94:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 1;
95:   UP_DMB();
96:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = other;
97:   UP_DMB();
98:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT);
99: 
100:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
101:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
102:     {
103:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
104:       UP_DMB();
105:       __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
106:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT);
107:       return false;
108:     }
109: 
110:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
111:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 1;
112:   UP_DMB();
113:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED);
114:   return true;
115: }
116: 
117: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
118: {
119:   (void)dev;
120:   __asm__ volatile("nop" ::: "memory");
121: }
122: 
123: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
124: {
125:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
126: 
127:   (void)dev;
128:   if (cpu >= 2 || g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != cpu + 1u ||
129:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == 0)
130:     {
131:       PANIC();
132:     }
133: 
134:   if (--g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth != 0)
135:     {
136:       UP_DMB();
137:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK |
138:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
143:   UP_DMB();
144:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
145:   UP_DSB();
146:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
147:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED);
148: }
149: 
150: const struct hwspinlock_ops_s g_bk7258_hwspinlock_ops =
151: {
152:   .trylock = bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock,
153:   .relax   = bk7258_hwspinlock_relax,
154:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock
155: };
156: 
157: void bk7258_hwspinlock_initialize(void)
158: {
159:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[0] = 0;
160:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[1] = 0;
161:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = 0;
162:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
163:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 0;
164:   UP_DSB();
165:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
166: }

56: static int bk7258_motor_button_worker(int argc, char **argv)

58:   struct pwm_info_s info =
59:   {

61:     .duty = BK7258_MOTOR_DUTY,

63:   bool candidate = false;
64:   bool pressed = false;

77:     }
78: 
79:   request_start = clock_systime_ticks();
80:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(BK7258_PM_CLK_CTRL_CMD,
81:                                 BK7258_PM_CLK_ID_PWM_1,
82:                                 BK7258_PM_CLK_POWER_UP, 0);
83:   if (ret < 0)
84:     {
85:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: PWM clock request failed: %d\n", ret);
86:       goto ready;
87:     }
88: 
89:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(200);
90:   syslog(LOG_INFO, "power-key motor: PWM clock transport wait=%d elapsed=%lu ms\n",
91:          ret, (unsigned long)TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - request_start));
92:   if (ret < 0)
93:     {
94:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: PWM clock ACK failed: %d\n", ret);
95:       goto ready;
96:     }
97: 
98:   nxsig_usleep(20000);
99:   fd = open("/dev/pwm0", O_RDWR);
100:   if (fd < 0)
101:     {
102:       ret = -errno;
103:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: open pwm0 failed: %d\n", ret);
104:       goto ready;
105:     }
106: 
107:   if (ioctl(fd, PWMIOC_SETCHARACTERISTICS,
108:             (unsigned long)(uintptr_t)&info) < 0)
109:     {
110:       ret = -errno;
111:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: set PWM characteristics failed: %d\n",
112:              ret);
113:       close(fd);
114:       goto ready;
115:     }
116: 
117:   ret = OK;
118: 
119: ready:
120:   g_motor_worker_result = ret;
121:   nxsem_post(&g_motor_ready_sem);
122:   if (ret < 0)
123:     {
124:       return ret;
125:     }
126: 
127:   printf("power-key motor worker ready, PWM parameters applied\n");
128: 
129:   for (;;)
130:     {
131:       bool sample = (board_buttons() & BUTTON_POWER_BIT) != 0;
132: 
133:       if (sample != candidate)
134:         {
135:           candidate = sample;
136:           samples = 1;
137:         }
138:       else if (samples < BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT)
139:         {
140:           samples++;
141:         }
142:

144:         {
145:           int cmd = candidate ? PWMIOC_START : PWMIOC_STOP;
146:           clock_t edge_start = clock_systime_ticks();
147: 
148:           if (ioctl(fd, cmd, 0) < 0)
149:             {
150:               syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: PWM cmd=%d failed: %d\n",
151:                      cmd, -errno);
152:               close(fd);
153:               return -errno;
154:             }
155: 
156:           pressed = candidate;
157:           syslog(LOG_INFO,
158:                  "power-key motor: button=%u, pwm cmd=%d applied elapsed=%lu ms\n",
159:                  candidate, cmd,
160:                  (unsigned long)TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - edge_start));
161:         }
162: 
163:       nxsig_usleep(BK7258_KEY_POLL_US);
164:     }

304:           goto errout_with_tcb;
305:         }
306: 
307:       /* Get the scheduler policy for this thread */
308: 
309:       policy = nxsched_get_scheduler(0);
310:       if (policy < 0)
311:         {
312:           errcode = -policy;
313:           goto errout_with_tcb;
314:         }
315:     }
316:   else
317:     {
318:       /* Use the scheduler policy and policy the attributes */
319: 
320:       policy                             = attr->policy;
321:       param.sched_priority               = attr->priority;
322: 
323: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
324:       param.sched_ss_low_priority        = attr->low_priority;
325:       param.sched_ss_max_repl            = attr->max_repl;
326:       param.sched_ss_repl_period.tv_sec  = attr->repl_period.tv_sec;
327:       param.sched_ss_repl_period.tv_nsec = attr->repl_period.tv_nsec;
328:       param.sched_ss_init_budget.tv_sec  = attr->budget.tv_sec;
329:       param.sched_ss_init_budget.tv_nsec = attr->budget.tv_nsec;
330: #endif
331:     }
332: 
333: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
334:   if (policy == SCHED_SPORADIC)
335:     {
336:       FAR struct sporadic_s *sporadic;
337:       sclock_t repl_ticks;
338:       sclock_t budget_ticks;
339: 
340:       /* Convert timespec values to system clock ticks */
341: 
342:       repl_ticks = clock_time2ticks(&param.sched_ss_repl_period);
343:       budget_ticks = clock_time2ticks(&param.sched_ss_init_budget);
344: 
345:       /* The replenishment period must be greater than or equal to the
346:        * budget period.
347:        */
348: 
349:       if (repl_ticks < budget_ticks)
350:         {
351:           errcode = EINVAL;
352:           goto errout_with_tcb;
353:         }
354: 
355:       /* Initialize the sporadic policy */
356: 
357:       ret = nxsched_initialize_sporadic(ptcb);
358:       if (ret >= 0)
359:         {
360:           sporadic               = ptcb->sporadic;
361:           DEBUGASSERT(sporadic != NULL);
362: 
363:           /* Save the sporadic scheduling parameters */
364: 
365:           sporadic->hi_priority  = param.sched_priority;
366:           sporadic->low_priority = param.sched_ss_low_priority;
367:           sporadic->max_repl     = param.sched_ss_max_repl;
368:           sporadic->repl_period  = repl_ticks;
369:           sporadic->budget       = budget_ticks;
370: 
371:           /* And start the first replenishment interval */
372: 
373:           ret = nxsched_start_sporadic(ptcb);
374:         }
375: 
376:       /* Handle any failures */
377: 
378:       if (ret < 0)
379:         {
380:           errcode = -ret;
381:           goto errout_with_tcb;
382:         }
383:     }
384: #endif
385: 
386:   /* Initialize thread local storage */
387: 
388:   ret = tls_init_info(ptcb);
389:   if (ret != OK)
390:     {
391:       errcode = -ret;
392:       goto errout_with_tcb;
393:     }
394: 
395:   /* Configure the TCB for a pthread receiving on parameter
396:    * passed by value
397:    */
398: 
399:   pthread_tcb_setup(ptcb, parent, trampoline, arg);
400: 
401:   /* Initialize the task control block */
402: 
403:   ret = pthread_setup_scheduler(ptcb, param.sched_priority, pthread_start,
404:                                 entry);
405:   if (ret != OK)
406:     {
407:       errcode = EBUSY;
408:       goto errout_with_tcb;
409:     }
410: 
411: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
412:   /* pthread_setup_scheduler() will set the affinity mask by inheriting the
413:    * setting from the parent task.  We need to override this setting
414:    * with the value from the pthread attributes unless that value is
415:    * zero:  Zero is the default value and simply means to inherit the
416:    * parent thread's affinity mask.
417:    */
418: 
419:   if (attr->affinity != 0)
420:     {
421:       ptcb->affinity = attr->affinity;
422:     }
423: #endif
424: 
425:   /* Join the parent's task group */
426: 
427:   group_join(ptcb);
428: 
429:   /* Set the appropriate scheduling policy in the TCB */
430: 
431:   atomic_and(&ptcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK);
432: 
433:   switch (policy)
434:     {
435:       default:
436:       case SCHED_FIFO:
437:         atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_FIFO);
438:         break;
439: 
440: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
441:       case SCHED_OTHER:
442:       case SCHED_RR:
443:         atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR);
444:         ptcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
445:         break;
446: #endif
447: 
448: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
449:       case SCHED_SPORADIC:
450:         atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC);
451:         break;
452: #endif
453:     }
454: 
455:   /* Return the thread information to the caller */
456: 
457:   if (thread != NULL)
458:     {
459:       *thread = (pthread_t)ptcb->pid;
460:     }
461: 
462:   /* Then activate the task */
463: 
464:   nxtask_activate(ptcb);
465: 
466:   return OK;
467: 
468: errout_with_tcb:
469: 
470:   /* Since we do not join the group, assign group to NULL to clear binding */
471: 
472:   ptcb->group = NULL;
473: 
474:   nxsched_release_tcb(ptcb, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
475:   return errcode;
476: }

123: static void pthread_start(void)
124: {
125:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb = this_task();
126:   FAR struct pthread_entry_s *entry =
127:     (FAR struct pthread_entry_s *)(ptcb + 1);
128:   pthread_startroutine_t pthread = ptcb->entry.pthread;
129:   pthread_trampoline_t trampoline = entry->trampoline;
130:   pthread_addr_t arg = entry->arg;
131: 
132:   /* The priority of this thread may have been boosted to avoid priority
133:    * inversion problems.  If that is the case, then drop to the correct
134:    * execution priority.
135:    */
136: 
137:   if (ptcb->sched_priority > ptcb->init_priority)
138:     {
139:       DEBUGVERIFY(nxsched_set_priority(ptcb, ptcb->init_priority));
140:     }
141: 
142:   /* Pass control to the thread entry point. In the kernel build this has to
143:    * be handled differently if we are starting a user-space pthread; we have
144:    * to switch to user-mode before calling into the pthread.
145:    */
146: 
147:   DEBUGASSERT(trampoline != NULL && pthread != NULL);
148: 
149: #ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT
150:   up_addrenv_leave_kernel();
151:   trampoline(pthread, arg);
152: #else
153:   up_pthread_start(trampoline, pthread, arg);
154: #endif
155: 
156:   /* The thread has returned (should never happen) */
157: 
158:   DEBUGPANIC();
159:   pthread_exit(NULL);
160: }

180:  *   This function initializes a Task Control Block (TCB) in preparation for
181:  *   starting a new thread.  It performs a subset of the functionality of
182:  *   task_create()
183:  *
184:  *   Unlike task_create():
185:  *     1. Allocate the TCB.  The pre-allocated TCB is passed in argv.
186:  *     2. Allocate the stack.  The pre-allocated stack is passed in argv.
187:  *     3. Activate the task. This must be done by calling nxtask_activate().
188:  *
189:  *   Certain fields of the pre-allocated TCB may be set to change the
190:  *   nature of the created task.  For example:
191:  *
192:  *     - Task type may be set in the TCB flags to create kernel thread
193:  *
194:  * Input Parameters:
195:  *   tcb        - Address of the new task's TCB
196:  *   name       - Name of the new task (not used)
197:  *   entry      - Application start point of the new task
198:  *   actions    - File action to be performed.
199:  *   attr       - Use attr set stacksize, stackaddr and priority.
200:  *   argv       - A pointer to an array of input parameters.  The array
201:  *                should be terminated with a NULL argv[] value. If no
202:  *                parameters are required, argv may be NULL.
203:  *
204:  * Returned Value:
205:  *   OK on success; negative error value on failure appropriately.  (See
206:  *   nxtask_setup_scheduler() for possible failure conditions).  On failure,
207:  *   the caller is responsible for freeing the stack memory and for calling
208:  *   nxsched_release_tcb() to free the TCB (which could be in most any
209:  *   state).
210:  *
211:  ****************************************************************************/
212: 
213: int nxtask_init(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, const char *name, main_t entry,
214:                 FAR const posix_spawn_file_actions_t *actions,
215:                 FAR const posix_spawnattr_t *attr,
216:                 FAR char * const argv[], FAR char * const envp[])
217: {
218:   int ttype = atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK;
219: #ifdef CONFIG_MM_TASK_HEAP
220:   size_t heapsize = attr->heapsize;
221: #else
222:   size_t heapsize = 0;
223: #endif
224:   int ret = OK;
225: 
226:   sched_trace_begin();
227: 
228: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PTHREAD
229:   /* Only tasks and kernel threads can be initialized in this way */
230: 
231:   DEBUGASSERT(tcb && ttype != TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
232: #endif
233: 
234: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
235:   /* Kernel threads do not own any address environment */
236: 
237:   if (ttype == TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_TASK)
238:     {
239:       FAR struct task_group_s *group =
240:         (FAR struct task_group_s *)(tcb + 1);
241: 
242:       if (group->tg_addrenv_own == NULL)
243:         {
244:           FAR struct addrenv_s *addrenv = addrenv_allocate();
245:           if (addrenv == NULL)
246:             {
247:               ret = -ENOMEM;
248:             }
249:           else
250:             {
251:               addrenv_attach(tcb, addrenv);
252:             }
253:         }
254:     }
255: 
256: #endif
257: 
258:   if (ret == OK)
259:     {
260:       /* Create a new task group */
261: 
262:       ret = group_initialize(tcb, atomic_read(&tcb->flags), heapsize);
263:       if (ret >= 0)
264:         {
265: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PTHREAD
266:           /* Initialize the task join */
267: 
268:           nxtask_joininit(tcb);
269: #endif
270: 
271: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_NOPREEMPT_KERNEL
272:           if (ttype == TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL)
273:             {
274:               /* Disable pre-emption for this task */
275: 
276:               tcb->lockcount = 1;
277:             }
278: #endif
279: 
280:           nxsem_init(&tcb->exit_sem, 0, 0);
281: 
282:           ret = task_setup(tcb, name, entry, actions, attr, argv,
283:                            envp, ttype);
284:           if (ret >= 0)
285:             {
286:               /* Now we have enough in place that we can join the group */
287: 
288:               group_postinitialize(tcb);
289:             }
290:           else
291:             {
292:               nxtask_joindestroy(tcb);
293: 
294:               nxsem_destroy(&tcb->exit_sem);
295: 
296:               group_leave(tcb);
297: 
298: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
299:               addrenv_drop(tcb->group->tg_addrenv_own, false);
300: #endif
301:             }
302:         }
303:     }
304: 
305:   sched_trace_end();
306:   return ret;
307: }

309: /****************************************************************************
310:  * Name: nxtask_uninit
311:  *
312:  * Description:
313:  *   Undo all operations on a TCB performed by task_init() and release the
314:  *   TCB by calling kmm_free().  This is intended primarily to support
315:  *   error recovery operations after a successful call to task_init()
316:  *   when a subsequent call to task_activate fails.
317:  *
318:  *   Caution:  Freeing of the TCB itself might be an unexpected side-effect.
319:  *
320:  * Input Parameters:
321:  *   tcb - Address of the TCB initialized by task_init()
322:  *
323:  * Returned Value:
324:  *   OK on success; negative error value on failure appropriately.
325:  *
326:  ****************************************************************************/
327: 
328: void nxtask_uninit(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb)
329: {
330:   irqstate_t flags;
331: 
332:   /* The TCB was added to the inactive task list by
333:    * nxtask_setup_scheduler().
334:    */
335: 
336:   flags = enter_critical_section();
337:   dq_rem((FAR dq_entry_t *)tcb, list_inactivetasks());
338:   leave_critical_section(flags);
339: 
340:   /* Release all resources associated with the TCB... Including the TCB
341:    * itself.
342:    */
343: 
344:   nxsched_release_tcb(tcb, atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK);
345: }

74:   /* Check if pre-emption is disabled for the current running task and if

77:    * also disabled.

83:        * g_pendingtasks task list for now.

85: 
86:       nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_pendingtasks());
87:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_PENDING;
88:       ret = false;
89:     }
90: 
91:   /* Otherwise, add the new task to the ready-to-run task list */
92: 
93:   else if (nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun()))
94:     {
95:       /* The new btcb was added at the head of the ready-to-run list.  It
96:        * is now the new active task!
97:        */
98: 
99:       DEBUGASSERT(rtcb->lockcount == 0 && !is_idle_task(btcb));
100:

102:       btcb->flink->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
103:       up_update_task(btcb);

119: /****************************************************************************
120:  * Name:  nxsched_switch_running
121:  *
122:  * Description:
123:  *   This function switches the head of the current CPU's assigned tasks
124:  *   list to the TCB given as parameter. The idle task is not switched out.
125:  *   If the running task can't be swapped out, the btcb is pushed to
126:  *   the ready-to-run list.
127:  *
128:  * Input Parameters:
129:  *   cpu          - Always this_cpu(). Given as argument only for
130:  *                  optimization
131:  *   switch_equal - When true, switch away a task of equal priority compared
132:  *                  to the pending one
133:  *
134:  * Returned Value:
135:  *   true if the currently active task is switched
136:  *
137:  * Assumptions:
138:  * - The caller has established a critical section
139:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
140:  *   was in.
141:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
142:  *   assigned tasks list has changed.
143:  *
144:  ****************************************************************************/
145: 
146: bool nxsched_switch_running(int cpu, bool switch_equal)
147: {
148:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
149:   int sched_priority = rtcb->sched_priority;
150:   FAR struct tcb_s *btcb;
151:   bool ret = false;
152: 
153:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu == this_cpu());
154: 
155:   if (nxsched_islocked_tcb(rtcb))
156:     {
157:       return false;
158:     }
159: 
160:   if (switch_equal && sched_priority > 0)
161:     {
162:       sched_priority--;
163:     }
164: 
165:   /* If there is a task in readytorun list, which is eglible to run on this
166:    * CPU, and has higher priority than the current task,
167:    * switch the current task to that one.
168:    */
169: 
170:   for (btcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
171:        btcb && btcb->sched_priority > sched_priority;
172:        btcb = btcb->flink)
173:     {
174:       /* Check if the task found in ready-to-run list is allowed to run on
175:        * this CPU. TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED may be used to override affinity. If
176:        * the flag is set, assume that btcb->cpu is valid, and it is the only
177:        * CPU on which the btcb can run.
178:        */
179: 
180:       if (CPU_ISSET(cpu, &btcb->affinity) &&
181:           ((btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) == 0 || btcb->cpu == cpu))
182:         {
183:           /* Found a task, remove it from ready-to-run list */
184: 
185:           dq_rem((FAR struct dq_entry_s *)btcb, list_readytorun());

733: ## 7. UART0 Mailbox V2 使用和边界
734: 
735: CP 启动后默认 owner 为 `CP_CLI`。只有 MB_UART0 STATE 成功 ACK、IPC power-up 和
736: PWC boot-ready 三个条件同时成立，且`bk_mb_uart_write_ready()`非零时，

738: reset/timeout都会清除门禁并请求回退到CP CLI。使用方式：
739: 
740: ```text
741: ap_console status
742: ap_console open
743: <RAW AP NSH interaction>
744: <press Ctrl-], release it, then press .>
745: ap_console status
746: ```
747: 
748: `open`在当前 CP CLI 响应经 UART TX-complete 后生效，并清 CP parser 和 UART RX；
749: RAW 模式不添加前缀。退出时按下`Ctrl-]`、松开，再按`.`；该转义不依赖行首状态。
750: 链路 reset/timeout/down 时自动清理
751: 未发送输入并回到 `CP_CLI`。`status`输出 owner/link/mode、bridge ring、MB_UART 状态、

**Conclusion**

The supplied `primary=48, secondary=13` snapshot points to a localized CPU0 scheduler/task-creation stall at `kthread_create("pwc", ...)`, not to a PWC mailbox transaction, PWC `0x5` ACK loss, worker-ready semaphore timeout, CPU2 affinity migration, or whole-chip hard freeze.

More precisely:

- `primary=48` is written immediately before creating the PWC kernel thread.
- The success-side return marker is `primary=51`.
- The PWC child’s first marker is `primary=49`.
- Neither side made observable progress after task activation began.
- `secondary=13` proves CPU2 completed its scheduler handoff and entered the idle loop.

The strongest interpretation is therefore a CPU0 freeze/deadlock inside generic NuttX task creation or activation, probably in an SMP scheduler/critical-section/atomic path. There is a smaller possibility that `kthread_create()` returned a negative errno and bringup exited while leaving stage 48 unchanged.

**Bringup Trace**

1. Early serial initializes logical mailbox state, Mailbox UART, physical MBOX0/IRQ79, and console registration at [bk7258_serial.c:224](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_serial.c:224), [bk7258_serial.c:243](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_serial.c:243), and [bk7258_serial.c:255](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_serial.c:255).

2. CPU2 performs raw mailbox boot notify/ping/ACK, enters the NuttX idle trampoline at [bk7258_cpustart.c:70](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:70), [bk7258_cpustart.c:77](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:77), and [bk7258_cpustart.c:80](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:80). Its first real idle call changes secondary 12 to 13 at [bk7258_idle.c:13](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_idle.c:13).

3. Board late initialization creates a detached, CPU0-affine bringup pthread at [bk7258_bringup.c:209](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:209) through [bk7258_bringup.c:221](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:221).

4. Bringup waits for the secondary scheduler, pins itself to CPU0, and creates `mbox-v2` and `mbox-diag` at [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1091](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1091), [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1102](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1102), and [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1118](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1118).

5. CPU0 SysTick is enabled only after those workers exist at [bk7258_bringup.c:74](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:74) and [bk7258_timerisr.c:63](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:63). The runtime CPU check rejects execution anywhere except logical CPU0 at lines 65–68.

6. Mailbox UART starts RESET/STATE probing, waits up to 8 seconds, and reaches link-ready at [bk7258_bringup.c:94](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:94) through [bk7258_bringup.c:111](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:111).

7. HW_CTRL command 1 is sent synchronously, CP completion ACK is required, and only then is `ipc-heartbeat` created at [bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:240](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:240) through [bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:259](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:259). Command 2 is queued on the two-second SysTick deadline at [bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:188](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:188) through [bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:220](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:220).

8. Bringup finally calls `bk7258_pwc_start()` at [bk7258_bringup.c:113](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:113) through [bk7258_bringup.c:124](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:124).

**Boottrace Interpretation**

The stage definitions are authoritative at [bk7258_boottrace.h:55](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_boottrace.h:55) and [bk7258_boottrace.h:74](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_boottrace.h:74):

- `primary=48`: `BK7258_BOOT_PWC_CREATE_ENTER`
- `primary=49`: PWC worker entered
- `primary=50`: PWC worker posted ready
- `primary=51`: parent returned from `kthread_create`
- `primary=52`: parent consumed worker-ready semaphore
- `primary=53`: parent is about to send PWC `0x5`
- `secondary=13`: CPU2 scheduler is running and CPU2 reached idle

The exact boundary is visible at [bk7258_pm_pwc.c:445](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:445) through [bk7258_pm_pwc.c:477](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:477). The worker-ready semaphore wait is after the missing stage 51, at lines 477–482. PWC `0x5` is later still, at [bk7258_pm_pwc.c:495](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:495).

Therefore this snapshot excludes:

- A wait on `g_worker_sem`
- PWC `0x5` send or ACK failure
- PSRAM power request/response
- PWC `0x11` commit
- CPU2’s previously documented stage-10 exception-return stall

Affinity is also unlikely: NuttX explicitly copies the parent affinity into a new kernel task at [task_setup.c:468](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_setup.c:468), while the parent was already CPU0-only. The PWC worker intentionally performs no late affinity migration at [bk7258_pm_pwc.c:327](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:327).

The repository does not contain the supplied latest serial capture or its five hexadecimal detail words. **Ranked Root Causes**

1. **CPU0 deadlock/stall in NuttX kernel-thread creation or activation: 75% confidence.**  
   `kthread_create()` allocates and initializes the TCB, then activates it synchronously at [task_create.c:77](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_create.c:77) through [task_create.c:124](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_create.c:124). Activation enters a scheduler critical section and may switch immediately to the higher-priority PWC worker at [task_activate.c:64](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_activate.c:64) through [task_activate.c:109](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_activate.c:109). Stage 48 with neither child stage 49 nor parent stage 51 localizes the stop to that path.

2. **`kthread_create()` returned a deterministic negative errno, but diagnostics leave stage 48 unchanged: 20% confidence.**  
   The code returns `pid` immediately on failure at [bk7258_pm_pwc.c:470](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:470), without recording the errno or a failure marker. This would make a clean startup failure look identical to a hang. `-ENOMEM` is possible but not strongly supported: the linked heap spans `0x280156d8..0x28064000`, over 320 KiB, according to the current map.

3. **PWC worker affinity or worker-ready semaphore defect: below 5% confidence.**  
   CPU2 is already stage 13; the parent is CPU0-affine; kernel threads inherit that affinity; the child posts readiness before blocking at [bk7258_pm_pwc.c:334](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:334); and the parent has not yet reached the semaphore wait.

4. **Mailbox/PWC transport failure: effectively excluded by this marker.**  
   No PWC command has been submitted at stage 48. CP remains in boot stage 4 until `0x5`, times out after 10 seconds, prints the trace, and rolls AP back at [pwr_clk.c:678](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:678) through [pwr_clk.c:723](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:723).

The failure is deterministic in where it stops, but the stop is best classified as a localized CPU0 task-creation/activation freeze, not a PWC affinity or semaphore protocol issue.
